title: TED: Keep Your Goals to Yourself
description: A 3-minute TED talk by Derek Sivers about why telling people your goals can stop you from reaching them. Note: contains one instance of mild language.

questions.prompt: Watch the talk. What is the main idea?

options.text: Telling people your goals can make you less likely to reach them.
You should always share your goals on social media.
Writing goals down is a waste of time.

questions.explanation: That's the surprising idea of the talk.

questions.prompt: Why can telling people a goal make it less likely to happen?

options.text: Your mind feels like the goal is already done.
Other people will steal your idea.

questions.explanation: Getting recognition feels like progress, so you're less motivated to do the hard work.

questions.prompt: In the experiment, how long could people work on their goal?
questions.explanation: They had 45 minutes to work toward their goal.

questions.prompt: What did the people who announced their goals do?

options.text: They stopped working after about 33 minutes.

questions.explanation: On average they stopped after 33 minutes.

questions.prompt: How did the people who kept their goals quiet feel at the end?

options.text: That they still had a long way to go.
That the test was too easy.

questions.explanation: They worked longer and felt there was still more to do.

options.text: Resist the temptation to announce your goals.
Tell everybody your goals every day.

questions.explanation: Or say them in a way that gives you no satisfaction yet.

questions.prompt: In the talk, "resist the temptation" means…

options.text: Don't do something you really want to do.

questions.explanation: Temptation = a strong wish to do something.
